correctness.rationale: Checked the exact S(2,m) adjacency (m-vertex clique in each row, cross-link (i,j)-(j,i) for i!=j). Any nonempty row forces >=m-k selected entries from its internal clique, while diagonal (i,i) ensures each row nonempty. A symmetric constant-row-sum-r matrix exists from cyclic near-neighbor shifts and optional diagonal. Equality forces all rows have size r and each chosen cross-link endpoint also chosen or it exceeds the neighbor cap k, hence symmetry; conversely every such matrix is feasible. Product (1+x_i)*prod(1+x_ix_j) counts diagonal and unordered offdiagonal decisions. Complement maps row r to m-r. Row r=1 represents involutions, row r=2 gives cycles and loop-ended paths. Independently enumerated full minimum subsets for m=3,4 and each k, agreeing with exact matrix counts 4,4 and 10,18,10. Universal proof handles all m and admissible k.
